funnel.step: BookNLP-processed cloze passage bank exists
funnel.why: BookNLP must successfully parse named entities from a book before any masked-name passage can be built at all.

funnel.step: Matched to filedata/book-level.csv (needs book_title, in_books3, num_ratings)
funnel.why: Every downstream regression needs Books3 membership and popularity; a book without that metadata can't be used no matter how good its passage bank is.

funnel.step: Original 6 models: run on the full matched corpus directly
funnel.why: Cheap/fast models (gpt-3.5, gpt-4o, claude, gemini, llama-8b, llama-70b) could be run at full scale, giving the highest-powered estimate of the Books3 effect.

funnel.step: New/incremental models: stratified sampling by in_books3 x popularity bucket, drawn without replacement across rounds
funnel.why: Newer models are far more expensive per call; stratifying keeps the Books3 x popularity cross-tab balanced even in a partial sample, so IV/pop-FE regressions stay estimable before the full corpus finishes.

name-cloze.excluded_note: 9 abandoned pilot files excluded (2-10 books each, never reaching full scale): gemini-2.5-pro x3, deepseek-v3, gpt-5.4 (non-mini), llama-3.3-70b x3, gemini-3.1-flash (100bk, folded into the flash-lite combined file), gemini-3.5-flash (41bk). Also dropped (2026-07-24): claude-opus-4-8, claude-sonnet-5, gpt-5.5 -- not part of the main model set and stuck at 494-989 books vs. the main set's full-corpus coverage, so no longer shown.

funnel.step: book-level.csv source
funnel.why: Starting universe of all books with usable metadata.

funnel.step: Nonfiction filter
funnel.why: Concepts/frameworks (as opposed to plot events) are a nonfiction-shaped unit of memorization; fiction is reserved for character-test instead.

funnel.step: Genre eligibility (LLM, cached)
funnel.why: Generalizes past messy OpenLibrary genre tags to find books that actually argue for ideas (vs. reference works, cookbooks, etc. with no extractable concept).

funnel.step: Concept discovery (extraction + recurrence >= 2 + validity)
funnel.why: Most prose is narrative or transitional, not concept-defining (~61% of extraction attempts are rejected); recurrence >= 2 stops a one-off phrase from being mistaken for a real coined framework, and validity screens out generic terms/proper nouns.

funnel.step: Originality cutoff (LLM score >= 3/5, infini-gram freq <= 5/B, local-corpus count <= 10)
funnel.why: Strong models scored ~100% on well-known nonfiction concepts before this filter — a sign the question was testing general world knowledge, not memorization of this specific book.

funnel.step: Verification (synthesis + centrality)
funnel.why: Rejects outright rather than falling back to a verbatim question, since synthesis (recombining book-specific ideas in a new way) is the only thing this bank is designed to test.

funnel.step: Assembly (dedup + quality + typing)
funnel.why: Final MCQ construction: distractors, question typing (standard/none-of-above/all-of-above).

funnel.step: Merge/dedupe on question_id
funnel.why: Removes exact-duplicate questions surfaced by overlapping discovery passes.

funnel.step: Final bank (concept_bank_final_combined.jsonl)
funnel.why: The book-and-question set actually evaluated against models.

concept-test.note: An earlier round (concept_bank_200_stratified.jsonl, 987 books, models gpt-4o / llama-3.3-70b / gemini-3.1-flash-lite, mixing verbatim+synthesis questions) is superseded by the current 1,748-book synthesis-only bank and is not shown here.

funnel.step: Book has a full-text .txt file
funnel.why: Extraction needs an actual passage to test against; unlike concept/character-test, both fiction and nonfiction are valid targets since no narrative or argumentative structure is required.

funnel.step: Word count >= ~3,000 words after trimming
funnel.why: Guarantees enough interior text to sample a 50-word prefix/suffix pair away from front matter.

funnel.step: Passage windows drawn from the 25th-75th percentile of word count
funnel.why: Avoids title pages, tables of contents, and back-matter (indices, ads) that would make for a degenerate or unrepresentative extraction test.

funnel.step: Stratified by in_books3 x popularity band (4 bands: 0-9 / 10-99 / 100-999 / 1000+)
funnel.why: Preserves the Books3 x popularity cross-tab this task's headline analysis needs — same rationale as name-cloze's incremental design.

funnel.step: Final random sample
funnel.why: The ~1,000-book random sample actually tested — deliberately the least-filtered of the four tasks, to measure raw extractability without a genre-suitability confound.

text-extraction.note: gpt-5.5 has complete coverage (4,855/4,855 pairs) on the canonical 1,000-book sample. gpt-4o and gpt-4o-mini have results only on smaller, earlier pilot tiers (200/2,925/30 pairs, not shown here since they don't share the canonical sample). No other model — and no Claude model at all — has been run on this task yet. No LLM-judge scores exist yet (all runs used --skip-judge).

funnel.step: SPL checkout rows, 2006-2025 (Seattle Open Data "Checkouts by Title")
funnel.why: Full public checkout export.

funnel.step: Filtered to checkoutyear 2019-2025 (matches Keepa panel window)
funnel.why: Keeps only the years overlapping the Keepa sales-rank panel and the Books3/ChatGPT treatment window.

funnel.step: Split by ISBN presence (ISBN only populated 2022+ in SPL's export)
funnel.remaining: 6,512,912 rows w/ ISBN (31,175 matched a book_id) / 7,916,781 without
funnel.why: Direct ISBN join only recovers 2022-2025; earlier years need fuzzy matching.

funnel.step: ISBN-less rows deduped to distinct (title, creator) candidates
funnel.why: Collapses repeated monthly rows of the same title before fuzzy matching, and bounds the matching problem to a tractable size.

funnel.step: Fuzzy title/author match (blocked by author surname, calibrated threshold)
funnel.why: Threshold chosen to hit ~95% precision, measured by holding out ISBN-confirmed books and checking whether title/author alone would have found them (82.9% recall at that threshold).

funnel.step: Combined with direct ISBN matches -> total matched books
funnel.why: Final checkout-demand sample. Matching is non-random -- skews toward popular, recent, fiction titles (see summary stats).

funnel.step: Restricted to books also present in the Keepa sales-rank panel
funnel.why: The comparison below needs the identical book sample on both sides, not just the same treatment/instrument.

books3-demand.note: Both regressions use the same design: treatment = books3, instrument = shares (a book's share of the Books3 corpus by publication year), Post cutoff = Nov 2022 (ChatGPT launch), book+month fixed effects where the spec is a panel. Sign convention differs by outcome: for Keepa sales rank, a positive coefficient means the book sells WORSE post-ChatGPT (substitution-consistent); for SPL checkouts, positive means MORE checkouts, so a substitution story predicts a NEGATIVE checkout coefficient. Checkout data itself only extends to Feb 2025 (a limit of SPL's current data export, not a chosen cutoff). 8,124 books present in both the SPL-checkout match and the Keepa sales-rank panel (97% of the 8,242 total checkout-matched books). Treatment = books3, instrument = shares (pub-year Books3-exposure share), Post cutoff = Nov 2022 (ChatGPT launch).

outcomes.text: Y_it = log(salesrank_it), the "min rank per month" variant: the lower (better-selling) of that book's paperback and hardcover median monthly Amazon rank. Panel is book_id x month_year, Jan 2019 - Dec 2025 (84 months), taken directly from the precomputed dv_min_rank_month_year column in keepa-analysis/data/keepa_salesrank_long.csv. Lower rank = more sales, so this is a log-rank outcome, not a log-sales outcome -- the sign convention below follows from that.

Y_it = log(1 + checkouts_it): checkouts_it is that book's total monthly SPL checkout count, summed across every matched format/edition (both direct-ISBN and fuzzy-matched rows). Panel is book_id x month_year, Jan 2019 - Feb 2025 (74 months -- SPL's export currently stops there, not a chosen cutoff). log1p (log(1+x) rather than log(x)) specifically because, unlike sales rank, checkout counts are genuinely zero in most book-months. Zero-filled: any month absent from the matched-checkout export is treated as a true zero, not missing data, since the matching pipeline only ever writes a row when >=1 checkout occurred that month -- averaging over only the observed months instead would overstate demand for infrequently-checked-out books.

equations.label: 1. Panel IV-TWFE (headline spec)
equations.note: W<sub>it</sub> = D<sub>i</sub> × Post<sub>t</sub> (endogenous: books3 × post-Nov-2022 indicator), instrumented by Z<sub>it</sub> = shares<sub>i</sub> × Post<sub>t</sub>. α<sub>i</sub> = book fixed effects, λ<sub>t</sub> = month fixed effects, both absorbed via alternating-projection (FWL) demeaning before 2SLS. SEs clustered by book. Identical equation for both outcomes -- only Y<sub>it</sub> differs.

equations.label: 2. + popularity × Post controls
equations.note: Same as (1), adding an interaction of Post with each Goodreads popularity-bin dummy (k ∈ {10-100, 100-1,000, 1,000+ ratings}, reference = 0-10) as additional exogenous regressors -- tests whether the effect is really books3, not just popular books trending differently after ChatGPT.

equations.label: 3. Cross-sectional IV (collapsed panel)
equations.note: Collapses the panel to one row per book (post-mean minus pre-mean, pre = Jan 2019-Oct 2022, post = Nov 2022 onward), then OLS and IV (D<sub>i</sub> instrumented by shares<sub>i</sub>) with popularity-bin dummies entering in levels (no Post interaction needed -- differencing already removes each book's own baseline level, so no book or month fixed effects are required here).

equations.label: 4. Callaway-Sant'Anna (CS) event-study DiD
equations.equation: ATT(g,t)  →  aggregated to overall ATT = E[Y<sub>it</sub>(g) − Y<sub>it</sub>(0) | G<sub>i</sub>=g]
equations.note: Doubly-robust, non-parametric DiD (Callaway & Sant'Anna 2021) against never-treated (non-books3) controls; one treatment cohort here (all books3 books treated at g = Nov 2022). Inference via 199-draw multiplier bootstrap, clustered by book. Deliberately NOT instrumented -- this is a plain treated-vs-control comparison, included as a check on whether the IV specs' identifying assumptions (relevance + exclusion of shares) are doing real work: a big gap between this and spec (1) is worth treating as a flag, not noise.

books3-demand.headline: Keepa's IV-TWFE shows a large, highly significant positive effect (substitution-consistent). The checkout IV-TWFE is a flat null -- small and insignificant across every estimator, not just a weaker version of the same effect. Plausible explanation: borrowing a library book is free, so LLM-substitution for the paid-purchase decision doesn't necessarily extend to the free-borrow decision.
